Public Portion 
 1. Discussion of the impact Spotted Lantern Flies have on Trees and Vegetation, and 
Preventative Measures. 
On October 14, 2026, the Health and Human Services Committee, chaired by Councilor Brian 
Santaniello, met to discuss the impact of spotted lantern flies on Springfield's trees and 
vegetation and potential preventive measures. City Forester Alex Sherman reported that 
Springfield first identified spotted lantern flies around 2022, and populations have increased 
significantly and spread citywide. He explained that the invasive pest primarily affects Tree of 
Heaven, grapevines, and fruit trees, potentially reducing fruit production, while posing a lower 
risk to established shade trees. 
 
The committee reviewed methods to reduce infestations, including removing the invasive Tree of 
Heaven and scraping egg masses from trees before they hatch in the spring. Sherman explained 
that complete eradication is unlikely, but preventive measures can help control local populations. 
Additional discussion addressed emerald ash borer infestations, beech leaf disease, and the City's 
ongoing tree replacement and planting efforts. The City planted approximately 1,000 trees in 
spring 2026, with another 750 anticipated for the fall. 
 
The committee requested that the City's Forestry website provide educational information on 
spotted lanternfly identification, prevention, and management. Sherman agreed to provide 
resources to help residents address infestations on their properties. No formal recommendations 
or votes were made. The meeting adjourned at 2:20 p.m.
